changelog: TERRAIN NOW BLOCKS SIGHT — for you and for them. Forest, hill and rock stop a sightline, so cover is somewhere to hide behind rather than just a damage modifier. Ranged fire obeys the same rule: no more shooting through a wood. HIGH GROUND IS THE ANSWER — stand on a hill and you see OVER the treetops, and further besides. The enemy is under exactly the same restriction, and their ordnance can no longer be aimed at ground they cannot currently see: break contact behind a treeline and the barrage stops following you to where you were. THE SNIPER is rebuilt around that. Sight 4, range 3, move 2, one shot a turn — it now sees exactly as far as it shoots, and no further. Take the hill and it sees 6 and shoots over the trees. At rank 5 it earns a second shot and armour-piercing rounds. THE TELEGRAPH TELLS THE TRUTH. An enemy with two actions in range hits TWICE, and the danger numbers said one — you braced for 4 and took 8. It also piled every swing onto one target: a 2-action enemy killing your soldier with the first blow does not put the second into the corpse, it turns to the next piece, which was never shown. The follow-up is now drawn as a dashed arrow to whatever it actually moves on to. Flanking is counted from where units WILL be standing, so two enemies converging each earn the bonus off the other's arrival. PIECES MOVE INSTEAD OF TELEPORTING. Infantry hop, armour glides at the speed of its own engine note. The fog lifts as a cloud that swells and thins rather than blinking out, and a battle opens under a closed board that is drawn back once you have read the briefing. FIXED, all found on a Mac: the volume dials never followed a drag on macOS at all — the desktop Settings panel is zoomed, and WebKit and Chromium disagree about what a zoomed element's on-screen rectangle is, so the dial was reading a pointer position tens of pixels from your actual finger. Unaffordable cards in hand kept their full-colour artwork instead of greying. The card collection took over a second to appear because it decoded every card face at once, including the eighty you had not scrolled to. Attack arrows and damage numbers drifted off their tiles if you moved the camera mid-animation. A kill two tiles off centre yanked the whole board across to centre it. Move markers at the edge of your vision were drawn underneath the fog. Panels in the Outpost sat against the left rail with a third of the frame empty. How to Play cropped the top off a column. ADDED: rest the pointer on any unit for two seconds for a stat breakdown. Space now accepts whatever is in front of you, as Escape cancels it. Still universal and still notarized: one download runs natively on Intel and Apple Silicon, and opens with no Gatekeeper warning.
